title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Ĝ is a profinite group, topologically generated by two elements ρ and σ (hypothesis (10a)). This is the 'loop equation' setting of the 2nd part of the Longue Marche notes. Typical cases are the profinite completion of the free group on two generators (π1 of P^1 minus 3 points) or quotients such as SL(2,Ẑ)/±1. The objects involved are:
- B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(Ĝ): the automorphisms u satisfying three conditions (6). These presumably are: u(ρ) conjugate to ρ, u(σ) conjugate to σ, and a condition on certain procyclic subgroups L_0, L_1 (generated by elements ε_0, ε_1).
- The map φ: u ↦ (ξ,η) = (u(ρ)ρ^{-1}, u(σ)σ^{-1}), with values in Σ_{ρ,σ} = {(ξ,η) : ξρ ~ ρ, ησ ~ σ, η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1}.
- φ is injective by (10a). Hypothesis (10b) says φ is surjective: every 'solution' (ξ,η) of the loop-type equation lifts to an automorphism u_{ξ,η} with u(ρ)=ξρ, u(σ)=ησ.

This page.
1. The group structure of B is transported to Σ. Since u'∘u(ρ) = u'(ξρ) = u'(ξ)ξ'ρ, the law is (13): (ξ',η')(ξ,η) = (u_{ξ',η'}(ξ)ξ', u_{ξ',η'}(η)η'). This is the same type of twisted composition law as Drinfeld's law on pairs (λ,f) in GT, where one 'cocycle' is inserted into the other.
2. Via int: Ĝ → Aut(Ĝ), the preimage of B_{ρ,σ} is said to be the centralizer N_0 of L_0 in Ĝ. Inner automorphisms automatically satisfy the two conjugacy conditions, so only the third condition, presumably u|L_0 = id, matters.
3. Goal: build a group G_{ρ,σ} that
   - contains (an image of) Ĝ as a normal subgroup,
   - receives B_{ρ,σ},
   - lets B act on Ĝ by conjugation exactly through its given automorphisms,
   - is generated by Ĝ and B.
   The aim is a 'Galois-type' extension group in which the GT-like group B and the geometric group Ĝ live together, analogous to π1 of the variety over Q versus the geometric π1 and Gal(Q̄/Q).
4. If Z(Ĝ) = 1, one simply takes the subgroup of Aut(Ĝ) generated by Inn(Ĝ) ≅ Ĝ and B. A crossed-out attempt used the semidirect product B·Ĝ and the map N_0 → B⋉Ĝ, g ↦ (int(g), g^{-1}).
5. Grothendieck rejects the trivial-centre hypothesis as unreasonable, e.g. for Ĝ = SL(2,Ẑ)/±1, whose centre ∏_p{±1}/±1 is huge. He then judges the introduction of N_0 ill-advised.

Continuation (next page). Take S_0G = B ⋉ Ĝ. Embed L_0 by g ↦ int(g^{-1})·g^{-1}; this is a normal subgroup, since it centralizes Ĝ and is B-equivariant. Put G_{ρ,σ} = S_0G / i(L_0). Then ker(Ĝ → G) = L_0 ∩ Z(Ĝ). This is the standard 'pushout along a crossed module' (relative holomorph) construction.
errors: No mathematical error. The law (13) checks out for composition u'∘u.

The claim that int^{-1}(B_{ρ,σ}) = centralizer of L_0 depends on condition (6) containing 'u acts trivially on L_0'. That condition is not visible on these pages, so it cannot be verified here; it is plausible.
SL(2,Ẑ)/±1 is not the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z), because the congruence subgroup property fails. It serves only as an example of a profinite group with nontrivial centre, which is correct.

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms parametrised by solutions (ξ,η) of a loop/conjugacy equation, with transported twisted composition law (13)
ideas.modern_name: Composition law on GT-type groups, pairs (λ,f)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the GT idea; these explicit computations are in the unpublished Longue Marche follow-up notes

ideas.what: Building a group containing Ĝ as a normal subgroup on which B acts by conjugation, as (B ⋉ Ĝ)/{(int(g)^{-1}, g^{-1}) : g ∈ L_0}, with kernel L_0 ∩ Z(Ĝ)
ideas.modern_name: Pushout / extension associated with the crossed module Ĝ → Aut(Ĝ); relative holomorph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory (Whitehead crossed modules; Eilenberg–MacLane extension theory)
ideas.where_published: Similar constructions occur in SGA1 / outer-action discussions; unsure about this specific form

ideas.what: The observation that trivial centre is an unreasonable hypothesis, e.g. for SL(2,Ẑ)/±1
ideas.modern_name: Centre-free versus non-centre-free profinite groups in anabelian/GT settings

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine group-theoretic steps in Grothendieck's GT-style study. They transport the group law to solutions of the loop equation and build an extension group, using a standard crossed-module quotient. Interesting as a record of how he set up the formalism, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'est qui sera unique par (10) -) )' should read '(et qui sera unique par (10 a)))'.
'On [-veut-] [-construit-] dans un groupe' is more likely 'On veut construire alors un groupe G_{ρ,σ}'.
'[?]itiv[?] B'_{ρ,σ}' is likely 'Plutôt/Initialement un B'_{ρ,σ}' (uncertain), followed by 'qui contiendra N_0'.
The crossed-out text contains 'B_{ρ,σ}·Ĝ (pr. semi/½ direct)' and the map 'N_0 → B_{ρ,σ}·Ĝ, g ↦ (int(g), g^{-1})'.
The final line is probably 'lequel on pratiquera ... ... ... ...)', continued on the next page with 'n'était pas très judicieuse'.
The page number at bottom left is 503, not 502.
